correctness.rationale: The exact quadrant identity has factor 64/R^4. Each axis contributes \(\pi bR\sin^2(aR)/2\) or its dual plus a \(\sqrt R\) Fresnel term; uniform-in-phase dominated convergence and oscillatory averaging control the remainder. The two Fresnel integrals both equal \(\sqrt{\pi a/2}\), yielding coefficient \(8\sqrt{2\pi}\). Bounded scaled-energy sequences force both axial phases to zero mod \(\pi\), and convergents to \(b/a\) produce matching upper limit; every parameter and quantifier is explicit. Finite numeric tests are only supplemental.
